speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, Building a Sustainable and Vibrant Community Arts Ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts strive to enrich the individual, encourage self-expression, while at the same time seeking to reach out, communicate and bring people together.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The National Arts Council (NAC) Arts and Culture Nodes at various venues island-wide energise and excite Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: A wide array of quality arts programmes, for people of all ages and walks of life, are available.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With the SG Arts Plan in place, the arts scene has been thriving, as artists chart professional careers and arts groups grow in strength.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I have three recommendations to build a sustainable and vibrant community arts ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Sharing resources, putting the same genre of performing arts under one roof.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, different hubs that are specifically designed for the music, theatre or dance groups will allow the groups to effectively share resources and rehearsal spaces.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The Stamford Arts House is a multidisciplinary arts centre with a focus on traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, the centre houses various professional arts companies of different art forms.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The Government can consider this: a shared acoustically treated recital hall for the orchestra and ensemble, a black box for theatre performances, dance theatre with treated flooring and height for dance companies.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will re-energise the building, and audiences just need to visit one particular location to watch the performance of a particular art form.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Earlier on, in September 2019, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng announced that Arts freelancers will have an arts resource website and will also have dedicated working spaces at Goodman Arts Centre and Stamford Arts Centre.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to this, perhaps we can also consider a central shared warehouse for the arts community, where props and sets can be stored, shared or reused.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is one of the ways we can do our part to save the Earth from climate change, reducing wastage and disposal issues.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Traditional media, such as the radio and television, still play an important role in sharing content and informing the public.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We used to have an arts radio station – Passion 99.5 FM.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Back then, the NAC launched this radio station on 31 December 1997 to increase awareness of the arts and provide the arts community with a public voice.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It featured magazine programmes on arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: However, the station was shut down in December 2003 because its listenership was too small to attract sustained sponsorship and advertising revenue to cover its operating costs.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Today, we have an increasing number in arts events and attendance.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We ought to deepen and further the reach of our performances and productions through the mainstream media.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: There is now a larger number of performing arts events offered over the years.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Also, more than 11 million attended non-ticketed arts and cultural events in 2017, an increase of nearly 20% from the year before and the highest turnout in seven years.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The content creators from mainstream radio stations and TV channels can even work hand in hand with the social media for audience development purposes and wider audience reach.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Partnership among schools, institutions and community arts groups establishes a vibrant and sustainable ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Community Clubs (CCs) can provide the space to support these alumni arts groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With these arts groups housed in the CCs, they can regularly engage in activities and perform, contributing back to the larger community.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The potential of working together among the arts groups is limitless.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With more collaboration opportunities, this will encourage and inspire these arts groups to reach the pinnacle of excellence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: However, I understand that a few CCs have closed down the arts groups housed in their venues.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: So, where will all these groups go to?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, since the Arts Council launched the SG Arts Plan, the number of arts professionals and arts groups has been increasing continuously.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With a thriving arts scene, people of all ages can enjoy arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Based on these developments, I hope the Government can better integrate resources and create more shared spaces so that we can further develop a vibrant arts ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: A recital hall, a dance studio and a black box for theatre performances can be put under one roof.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Audiences just need to visit one location to watch different genres of arts performances.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is not only convenient in terms of location selection, but also conducive for interaction and exchange.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The Stamford Arts House is a multidisciplinary arts centre with a focus on traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It has drawn traditional arts groups to base there.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Siong Leng Musical Association, Ding Yi Music Company, Indian dance groups and Malay modern dance groups are located at the centre.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In September 2019, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng announced that arts freelancers would have an arts resource website, and there will be two co-working spaces.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to these, perhaps the Government can consider a chamber music recital hall and piano rooms with sound insulation facilities in the music centre.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In the dance and theatre centre, we can have a black box and a dance studio and even a common storeroom for props which can be reused.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will help reduce wastage and is environmentally friendly.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We can set up a shared warehouse to house props and sets.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: By doing so, spaces can be used more efficiently and sustainably, and it is good for the environment by cutting wastage.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The mainstream media can play an important role in promoting different arts genres.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, I suggest that we revisit the plan to reinstate the arts radio and TV channel.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Besides traditional media, content creators for mainstream radio stations and TV channels can even work hand in hand with the social media team for wider reach.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These are critical for audience development and the development of our arts scene.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, foster and further the collaboration between CCs and schools.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: CCs gather people of different ages and backgrounds together.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, it is a good place to promote arts, allowing community arts to join hands with school arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The establishment of alumni arts groups will be a win-win situation for multiple parties, for example, symphony orchestras, Chinese orchestras, dance groups and theatre groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The CCs can be the extension and complement of the school arts scene, providing a good arts platform for the residents.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With more collaboration opportunities, arts groups can exchange ideas, work and explore together, and become more creative.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will make the whole arts scene more vibrant and dynamic.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It will take a long time to build an arts ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We should not only bring arts to the people, but also allow Singapore’s arts community to groom more top-notch arts professionals.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To that end, we must build a vibrant community arts ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): With the mainstream media’s support, having shared resources for performing arts of different genres, as well as partnership between community arts groups and schools, these help to achieve synergy to build a vibrant community arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and our cultural institutions recognise the importance of fostering the sustained and sustainable growth of Singapore’s arts and culture over the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have been and are committed to working closely with partners from the private and people sectors towards this end.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will start by addressing Mr Terence Ho's first and third suggestions on the use of spaces for the arts and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I agree that it is important to ensure efficient use of physical spaces in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Venues, such as the Goodman Arts Centre (GAC), Stamford Arts Centre (SAC), Aliwal Arts Centre, and the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre, currently provide our arts community with many creation and presentation spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, demand for art spaces continues to increase and remains high.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Multi-purpose studios, performance venues, office spaces and storage rooms are co-shared at our arts centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This arrangement not only maximises available spaces but also allows the arts community to strengthen their networks, facilitate exchange of ideas, and increase opportunities for collaboration and partnership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, the GAC offers arts practitioners the use of facilities, such as a Black Box, dance studio and acoustically-treated music studios.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: GAC's multidisciplinary tenant mix was a purposeful design by NAC to catalyse diverse and quality artistic works, create greater synergies and collaborations amongst the various art forms, and introduce appreciation of different art forms and genres to audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Today, GAC is an energetic arts enclave, drawing in the public interested in experiencing the diverse range of art forms and arts activities on offer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We agree with Mr Terence Ho's suggestion that NAC can grow the Stamford Arts Centre's potential to similarly develop into a vibrant and attractive arts venue with the mix of performing arts groups which share its spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will continue to review arts spaces under its care and will prioritise shared and common spaces that benefit more groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Mr Terence Ho mentioned, there are two co-working spaces for arts freelancers at GAC and SAC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They will be officially launched in the coming weeks, which would further contribute to the dynamism of our arts spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Given our limited arts GFA, however, we would also encourage our arts practitioners to consider how they can pool their resources to rent commercial spaces, or for members in the arts community with existing facilities to open them up for sharing with or rental to others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Aside from arts spaces under NAC, we also work closely with corporate and community partners to unlock new space for arts practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One such partner is the Urban Redevelopment Authority, which encourages developers to allocate space in malls for arts, sports and social groups with strong community links through its Community Sports Facilities Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arts groups like Wild Rice, Singapore Dance Theatre and The Rice Company Limited are examples of organisations that have successfully benefited from this scheme through retail operators like CapitaLand, Far East Organisation and Frasers Centrepoint.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that more developers and venue owners could support this scheme and provide space for artists to flourish and contribute to their communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho would be familiar with community orchestras and bands that have been formed and housed at our CCs, such as Keat Hong Chinese Orchestra at the Chua Chu Kang CC and West Winds at the Bukit Batok CC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These groups are dedicated to developing young talents and are useful platforms for many to continue pursuing their passions even after leaving school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NAC also works with the People’s Association (PA) to facilitate co-location of arts groups within community facilities, such as Our Tampines Hub and Wisma Geylang Serai.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Mr Terence Ho noted, the arts groups in such venues can contribute to the vibrancy of their neighbourhoods and grow their community stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC and PA are open to considering more of such co-location opportunities if there is a good fit between our CCs and the needs, priorities and commitment of arts groups, including alumni arts groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On their part, arts groups should be responsive and adaptive to the needs of local audiences and community stakeholders, such as grassroots organisations and space owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I agree with Mr Terence Ho that it is important to promote the arts to as wide an audience as possible and to give everyone the opportunity to experience our vibrant culture and for it to become a part of all Singaporeans’ lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC already works with mainstream media platforms to showcase the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, Mediacorp, as our national broadcaster, continues to make arts content accessible and enjoyable to the public across its free-to-air and digital platforms, where appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arts and culture-related programming that have been broadcast recently include SPOP Sing!, Lights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Singapore, and Singapore Talent Night, which showcased performances by local artists who performed at River Hongbao 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC will continue to explore opportunities to work with mainstream media to reach out to radio and TV audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, with the increasingly widespread use of technology, coupled with global trends on declining TV viewership and radio listenership, it is important to also tap on digital platforms and channels to complement traditional media to transform the way in which audiences engage with our arts and culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through such initiatives, we seek to bring our arts and culture to new audiences while simultaneously engaging existing audiences in new and meaningful ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This can range from developing audiences to appreciate their work, to creating new works of art which can appeal to a wider audience and continually enhancing their governance and financial processes to attract and retain donors and sponsors.
